wu: Fruit Charades: Teacher acts out a fruit (e.g., peeling a banana), students guess 'Is it a banana?' and the class responds 'Yes, it is!' or 'No, it isn!'
wuAlt: Fruit Memory Game: Students match picture and word flashcards for fruits, saying 'Apple' when they find a pair
Fruit I Spy: Teacher says 'I spy with my little eye something red and round', students guess 'Is it an apple?'
pres: Teacher shows real fruits or large flashcards of apple, banana, orange, grapes, strawberry, lemon, saying 'This is an apple. I like apples.' Students repeat. Teacher asks 'Do you like apples?' and models 'Yes, I do' or 'No, I don't'. Students point to thumbs up/down to show understanding.
presAlt: Fruit Story: Teacher reads a simple story about a monkey who likes bananas but not lemons, using target language
Fruit Bingo Prep: Teacher calls out fruits, students mark them on a bingo grid, saying 'I like grapes' when they mark
prac: Fruit Likes Survey: Students walk around with a paper asking 'Do you like apples?' to 3 friends, tick yes/no, and report back to teacher 'Ali likes apples. Fatima doesn't like lemons.' Teacher provides sentence frames on the board.
pracAlt: Fruit Dominoes: Students match picture cards to word cards, saying 'Apple' when they place a card
Fruit Board Game: Students roll a dice, move a counter, and say 'I like/ don't like [fruit]' when they land on a square
ls: Fruit Listening Bingo: Teacher calls out 'I like strawberries' or 'I don't like lemons', students cover the corresponding picture on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
re: Fruit Relay: Two lines of students race to the board, draw a fruit, and run back. Team with most correct drawings in 2 minutes wins.
prod: Make a Mini-Book: Students fold 3 sheets of paper into a book, draw 6 fruits on each page, write 'I like ___' or 'I don't like ___' under each, and read it to a partner using a pointer.
rw: Trace and Copy: Students trace fruit words from a worksheet, then copy them into sentences. Advanced learners write 'I like apples. I don't like lemons.' with a drawing.
st: Read 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar' focusing on fruit pages, then sing 'Apples and Bananas' song replacing vowels. End with Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students act out fruits for others to guess
Students match picture and word cards for fruits
Teacher calls out likes/dislikes, students cover pictures
Teams race to draw fruits on the board
Ask friends about likes and report back
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short story about a fruit monster who likes all fruits
Support: Use word banks with pictures for writing sentences
hw: Draw 3 fruits and write 'I like ___' or 'I don't like ___' under each
Make a fruit collage and label each fruit
Interview your family about fruit likes and write down 3 answers
tip: Use real fruits when possible to engage tactile learners and build vocabulary retention through multisensory input.
